turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you. Well, honestly, what brings me in is this... this constant restless feeling I’ve been having. It’s hard to explain, but it’s like I’m wound way too tight all the time, and I just can’t fully settle down. 

And it’s really frustrating because it happens even when I’m supposed to be calmly sitting and focusing. Like, I’m a wholesale buyer, so a big part of my job involves these long, intensive planning meetings where we’re going over seasonal catalogs, negotiating with vendors, looking at margins... and I’m supposed to just sit there at the conference table, but I feel this tension, almost like a motor running inside me. I just can't get comfortable. 

But it’s not just at work, either. I try to do relaxing things in my downtime to unwind, you know? I like to paint, so I’ll get all my supplies out, mix my colors, and set up my easel in the sunroom, thinking I’m going to have this nice, quiet, peaceful afternoon, but I just can't settle into the actual painting. I feel like I need to be doing something else. Or even yoga! I signed up for this yoga class because everyone always says it’s exactly what you need to center yourself and relax, right? So I'll be there on the mat, and the instructor is telling us to do our deep breathing and find our stillness, and my body just feels completely restless the whole time. I'm just lying there feeling wound up. It’s just this constant, humming inability to just be still, and I don't really know how to turn it off...

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly reports a 'constant restless feeling' and an inability to fully settle down.
symptom_reasoning.S013: The patient describes an inability to settle into or be still during relaxing leisure activities like painting and yoga.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes feeling 'almost like a motor running inside me,' which is a classic presentation of being driven by a motor.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient describes feeling 'wound way too tight' and experiencing 'tension,' indicating feeling keyed up or on edge.

turns.doctor_question: Has this feeling of being unable to sit still been present for most of your life, or is this something that has only started bothering you more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Well, you know, it's interesting you ask that, because when I really think about it, I guess I've always been a little high-energy, maybe a bit of a fidgeter, but it was never really a problem, you know? Like, it never interfered with my life or made me feel this... this intensely wound-up way. But as for this specific feeling, this constant, unmanageable restlessness where I just absolutely cannot settle down no matter what I do? That's definitely more recent. 

I can actually pinpoint it pretty well, because it's been noticeably harder to manage for about two years and two months now. And I know the timeline so exactly because that’s right around the time when all these conflicts with my in-laws really started escalating and just completely taking over our lives. It’s a whole long story, but basically, there were all these disagreements about boundaries and family obligations, and it just turned into this massive, ongoing stressor. And it felt like every single evening, instead of coming home and unwinding from work, my husband and I would be dealing with phone calls, or texts, or just rehashing the latest drama with his parents. 

So our evenings, which used to be my time to recharge, just became this battleground of stress. And it was right around then, about two years and two months ago, that I started noticing this restless motor feeling really kicking into high gear. It’s like my body just absorbed all that tension from the family drama and never let it go, and now I just can't turn it off, even when the in-laws aren't actively causing a crisis. It's just always there now.

turns.doctor_question: Beyond the stress involving your in-laws, do you find yourself feeling excessively anxious or worried about many other different areas of your life, such as your work performance, your health, or your finances?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, not really. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting around worrying about everything under the sun, you know? Like work... I mean, sure, the catalog meetings are long and I get all restless sitting there, but I'm actually really good at my job. I've been doing this for a long time, and I know how to spot a trend and negotiate a good margin, so I don't really stress about my performance. My boss is happy with me, my reviews are always solid. And finances... well, we're doing okay. We're not rich, but we pay our bills and we have some savings, so I'm not lying awake at night panicking about money. 

And health... well, I mean, other than this weird, constant motor running inside me that I can't seem to shut off, I feel physically fine. I go to my checkups, my blood pressure is normal, all that stuff. It's really just... it's just this physical inability to settle down. It's not like my brain is spinning with a million worst-case scenarios about my life. It's more like my body is just trapped in this state of high alert, especially since all that stuff with the in-laws started. It's like the stress of that specific situation just flipped a switch in my nervous system, and now I just can't physically relax, even when there's nothing specific I'm actually worrying about at that exact moment. It's so frustrating because I'll be trying to paint or do yoga, and my mind isn't racing with anxious thoughts about work or money, but my body is just buzzing, like I need to jump up and run a mile or something. So, no, it's not a general worry about everything. It's just... this physical feeling.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from this internal restlessness, do you experience any specific physical sensations, such as chronic aches, muscle tightness in a particular area, or a feeling of a 'lump' in your throat?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, not really. I mean, I don't have any kind of chronic aches or pains, thank goodness. My joints are fine, my back is fine, I don't get those terrible tension headaches that some people get when they're stressed. And I definitely don't have that lump in the throat feeling you mentioned. I know exactly what you mean by that, though, because my sister gets that when she's upset—she says it feels like she swallowed a golf ball and it just got stuck halfway down. But no, I don't get that at all. 

As for muscle tightness... I mean, maybe a little bit in my shoulders sometimes? But honestly, I think that's just from sitting at a computer for so much of the day. You know how it is when you're typing emails and reviewing spreadsheets for hours on end, you kind of hunch over without realizing it, and then by the end of the day your neck and shoulders are just stiff. I think everyone gets that, right? Especially in my line of work where you're just staring at screens and catalogs all day. But it's not like this intense, painful knot or anything. It's just normal stiffness. 

So, yeah, it's really not about aches or pains or weird physical sensations like a lump in my throat. It all just comes back to that... that motor feeling. That buzzing. It's not painful, it's just incredibly annoying and persistent. It's like my muscles aren't necessarily tight, they're just... ready to go. Like a runner at the starting block waiting for the starting pistol, you know? Just this constant, low-level physical anticipation that never actually resolves into anything. So I don't feel achy, I just feel... revved up. All the time.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find that you are often irritable, or that you have difficulty falling or staying asleep since this restlessness began?
turns.patient_response:
Irritable? You know, people always assume that if you're keyed up, you must be snapping at everyone, but honestly, no, I wouldn't say I'm irritable at all. In my job, dealing with wholesale vendors and negotiating margins all day, if I were irritable, I'd lose all my best suppliers in a heartbeat. You have to keep a good relationship, you have to be pleasant, so I've always been pretty even-tempered. Even with all that in-law drama I mentioned earlier—which, believe me, is enough to make anyone completely lose their temper—I'm usually the peacekeeper. My husband is the one who gets irritable about it, he'll get short with people or start pacing around the kitchen, but I don't get angry or snappy. I just get that internal buzzing feeling. 

And as for sleep... you know, it's actually really surprising, but no, I don't have any trouble sleeping whatsoever. You would think with this invisible motor running all day long, I'd be staring at the ceiling at 2 AM, but I actually fall asleep right away. I think it's because by the time 10:30 or 11:00 rolls around, my body is just so physically exhausted from... well, from containing all this restless energy all day long, you know? I do my little nighttime routine, wash my face, maybe try to read a few pages of a book in bed—though honestly, lately I usually just read the same paragraph over and over because I can't quite settle into it—but once the lights actually go out and I close my eyes? I'm out like a light. 

I sleep right through the night, usually completely uninterrupted, right up until my alarm goes off at 6:15. I don't toss and turn, I don't wake up in a panic. So, yeah, it's strange, but my sleep is completely fine, and my mood is fine. I'm not grumpy, I'm not sleep-deprived. It really is just that daytime physical revved-up feeling that won't leave me alone.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that your level of distress, specifically this constant buzzing sensation, is significantly more intense than what would normally be expected given the situation with your in-laws?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, not really... I mean, I don't think so? It's hard to gauge what "normally expected" is, you know, because everyone handles family drama differently. But the thing with my in-laws... it's not just a minor disagreement about where to spend the holidays. It's been this ongoing, really intense conflict over some property and estate stuff, and it's been dragging on for months. There are lawyers involved now, and my mother-in-law is constantly calling and leaving these incredibly passive-aggressive voicemails, and my husband's brother is completely stonewalling us... it's a mess. A total, stressful mess.

So when you ask if my reaction is out of proportion... I honestly don't think it is. I think anyone dealing with this level of family toxicity and legal threats would feel completely wound up. It's like, how could you not be? It's a huge deal. It threatens our financial security, it threatens my husband's relationship with his entire family... it's not just a little spat. So, honestly, the fact that my body is reacting this way, this constant buzzing and feeling like a motor is running... it feels like a pretty natural physical response to a really unnatural, highly stressful situation. 

I mean, if this were just about, I don't know, a disagreement over a catalog layout at work, then yeah, I'd say feeling this physically revved up would be totally crazy and out of proportion. But given everything that's happening with his family? I think my body is just doing what it's supposed to do when it's under an immense amount of pressure. It's just... it's just really uncomfortable to live with day in and day out, you know? But no, I wouldn't say the intensity is more than what you'd expect for this specific nightmare we're dealing with. It feels pretty proportional to the mess itself.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly describes experiencing a 'constant buzzing and feeling like a motor is running'.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient describes feeling 'completely wound up' and 'physically revved up' in response to the stress.
